root_cause.text: The driver uses BUG_ON assertions to validate fence writeback address alignment inside a code path reachable from unprivileged userspace via DRM_IOCTL_AMDGPU_CS, allowing a user to deliberately trigger a kernel panic.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces BUG_ON(addr & 0x3) with WARN_ON(addr & 0x3) in sdma_v4_0_ring_emit_fence. The commit message states "These assertions can be reached from unprivileged userspace via crafted DRM_IOCTL_AMDGPU_CS submissions, causing a fatal kernel panic in a scheduler worker thread."

intent_record.intent_summary: Downgrade from BUG_ON to WARN_ON for misaligned address in SDMA fence emission to avoid kernel panic, while still alerting of potential issues.
intent_record.what: Replaced BUG_ON with WARN_ON in sdma_v4_0_ring_emit_fence for address alignment check.
intent_record.how: Previously, if the address had lower two bits set (misaligned), the kernel would panic. Now it prints a warning and continues execution.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reduce severity of alignment check from fatal BUG to non-fatal WARN to avoid crashing the system on recoverable conditions.
intent_record.what: Replaced BUG_ON with WARN_ON in the condition checking alignment of the address in sdma_v4_0_ring_emit_fence.
intent_record.how: Previously, an unaligned address (lower 2 bits non-zero) would trigger a kernel BUG (crash). Now it only prints a warning and continues execution.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability by downgrading the alignment check from a fatal BUG_ON to a non-fatal WARN_ON, preventing a user-triggerable kernel panic in the DRM_IOCTL_AMDGPU_CS path.

candidates.rationale: BUG_ON assertion triggers kernel panic on misaligned address, reachable from unprivileged userspace via DRM_IOCTL_AMDGPU_CS, allowing denial-of-service.
